items.title: Exact background-coupled RG comparison
items.design_state: A-page finite-regulator definition of an exact background-coupled Wilsonian comparison with fixed symmetry, background groupoid, field content, measure, and local-counterterm relation; no continuum existence claim.
items.statement:
Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$. Fix an integer $d\geq1$, a compact smooth oriented Euclidean $d$-manifold $M$ with no boundary, its tangential structure (including a spin structure when the fields require one), and the model's boundary conditions. Let $\Gamma$ be its chosen finite regulator graph. Fix a compact internal symmetry group $G$ with its actual global form and its action on every retained and integrated field multiplet. The symmetry is global, not a dynamical gauge redundancy. A **background groupoid** $\mathscr B$ is a category in which every arrow is invertible; its objects are the admitted nondynamical $G$-background data and its arrows are exactly the permitted background gauge transformations, including large transformations when the model admits them. The background data, groupoid objects and arrows are part of the model input.

At each positive Wilsonian scale $\mu$ in a fixed interval $0<\mu_{\mathrm{IR}}<\mu_{\mathrm{UV}}$, a regulated model supplies its actual finite-dimensional field configuration space $\Phi_\mu$, Borel measure $\nu_\mu$, dimensionless action $S_\mu(\phi;b)$ for $\phi\in\Phi_\mu$ and $b\in\mathscr B$, and finite nonzero background partition functional

$$
Z_\mu[b]=\int_{\Phi_\mu}e^{-S_\mu(\phi;b)}\,d\nu_\mu(\phi).
$$

All field representations, the regulator, measure normalizations, and background boundary conditions are fixed data. The local effective functional is $W_\mu[b]=-\log Z_\mu[b]$ on each common nonzero background patch; its transition phases on overlaps are retained.

An **exact background-coupled RG comparison** from $\mu_{\mathrm{UV}}$ to $\mu_{\mathrm{IR}}$ consists of exact Wilsonian high-coordinate integrations as in the supplied finite-regulator Wilsonian-action definition, equivariant under every arrow of $\mathscr B$, with all surviving low-energy fields and topological sectors included at the infrared endpoint. It also specifies one single-valued, admissible, dimensionless local background counterterm $C[b]$ for which

$$
W_{\mu_{\mathrm{UV}}}[b]-W_{\mu_{\mathrm{IR}}}[b]=C[b]
$$

in each common local branch and compatibly on overlaps. Here local means an integral or finite-regulator sum of densities depending on background data and finitely many derivatives or neighboring cochains; the allowed counterterm space is fixed as part of the model. This definition records a finite-regulator flow interface and its locality hypothesis. It does not assert that such a flow exists for an arbitrary continuum QFT or that any continuum limit exists.

items.title: Symmetry-preserving RG anomaly matching
items.design_state: A-page conditional equality of the selected anomaly class along the declared exact symmetry-preserving background flow, modulo the stated local counterterms and global holonomies; no phase exclusion or continuum claim.
items.statement:
Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$. Fix a finite-regulator model on a compact, closed, oriented Riemannian spin four-manifold $M$, with its actual boundary-condition data, fields and jets, regulator, measure, and admissible local counterterms at every scale. Let $G$ be a compact internal global symmetry group with fixed global form, a smooth principal right $G$-bundle $P\to M$, background connection $A$, and unitary finite-dimensional representation $R$. The admitted background groupoid has these nondynamical connections as objects and the selected background gauge transformations as arrows; the symmetry is exact and unbroken along the flow and is not a dynamical gauge redundancy. Fix a smooth family of Fredholm chiral Dirac operators $D^+_{A,R}$ and its inverse determinant line with the Quillen metric and Bismut–Freed unitary connection, as in the determinant-line definition. On each background patch, the finite-regulator partition functional at scale $\mu$ is the local scalar representative of a section of that line, and its transition functions and endpoint gauge actions are retained.

Also fix a Minkowski coordinate region $U\subseteq\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with its orientation, spin structure, boundary-term convention, fields and jet domains, and identify it with the Euclidean local-variation problem by a specified Wick-rotation map. Use its background-only finite-jet BRST complex, with nilpotent differential $s$ and horizontal derivative $d_H$; its local anomaly class is the relative cohomology class of ghost-number-one horizontal four-form cocycles modulo $d_H$ and the declared four-dimensional background counterterms. Write $\mathcal C_{\mathrm{loc}}$ for the local density whose integral is the counterterm $C$. Assume an exact symmetry-preserving Wilsonian comparison from $\mu_{\mathrm{UV}}$ to $\mu_{\mathrm{IR}}$ retains all remaining low-energy and topological sectors and satisfies $W_{\mu_{\mathrm{UV}}}[A]-W_{\mu_{\mathrm{IR}}}[A]=C[A]$ on each common local branch, for one admissible, single-valued, dimensionless local counterterm. For the determinant-line comparison, take $C$ in the unitary phase convention so $e^{-C[A]}\in U(1)$. Assume the line-valued comparison induces a unitary isomorphism of the endpoint determinant-line families which, in local frames, is multiplication by the phase $e^{-C[A]}$ and which preserves the specified unitary connections and endpoint gauge identifications. Then the ultraviolet and complete infrared four-dimensional local BRST anomaly classes agree modulo the declared local counterterms, and the determinant-line holonomies agree on every admitted loop of background connections modulo gauge transformations. This is a conditional matching constraint only; it determines no infrared spectrum or gap and asserts no continuum limit or empirical result.

items.title: Anomaly matching structures for fusion 2-categories
items.design_state: Status-reviewed bounded 2+1d bosonic fusion-2-category anomaly-matching classification question; the earlier 3+1d/fusion-2-category lead is corrected to the dimension supported by the current sources.
items.statement:
Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$. Fix an oriented bosonic $2+1$-dimensional theory and an exact all-boson finite semisimple fusion 2-category symmetry $\mathcal C$ over $\mathbb C$, using the earlier Gray-monoid convention, adjoints, tensor duals and split separable monads. Objects, 1-morphisms and 2-morphisms label surface defects, line junctions and point junctions respectively. All-boson type here means the class obtainable by generalized gauging from a finite ordinary group $G$, possibly with anomaly $[\omega]\in H^4(BG;U(1))$: stack an $H$-symmetric three-dimensional topological theory for a finite subgroup $H\leq G$ and gauge diagonal $H$, with its anomaly canceled in the stacked system. Retain the full stacked theory, including nonminimal choices; it need not be an invertible phase. Fix a particular symmetry-boundary realization $B_{\mathcal C}$ in the $3+1$-dimensional symmetry topological field theory $Z(\mathcal C)$. Different boundaries realizing an equivalent abstract symmetry category are not silently identified.

Consider marked diagrams $\mathcal N\xrightarrow{I}\mathcal C\xrightarrow{P}\mathcal S$ of finite semisimple monoidal 2-categories and linear monoidal 2-functors, together with chosen symmetry boundaries $B_{\mathcal N},B_{\mathcal S}$, gapped interfaces $\mathcal I_I,\mathcal I_P$ between their SymTFTs, and specified identifications of each transported source symmetry boundary with the corresponding target symmetry boundary (the source's Matching Equation). The marking includes the object, junction and point-junction transport, their composition and tensor coherences, and all endpoint spaces and composition maps of bulk defects on the boundaries and interfaces. An endpoint is an allowed boundary or interface junction terminating a bulk topological defect. Two such marked diagrams are equivalent when monoidal 2-equivalences of $\mathcal N$ and $\mathcal S$, the identity of the fixed marked $\mathcal C$, invertible monoidal transformations of the two functors, and equivalences of the interfaces and endpoint data intertwine all these markings and coherences. This is not equality merely of lists of defect labels.

Classify the equivalence classes of such diagrams that realize higher anomaly-matching sequences in the following operational sense suggested by the SymTFT construction: every defect endable on $B_{\mathcal C}$ is endable on $\mathcal I_I$; the only sectors endable both on $B_{\mathcal C}$ and on $\mathcal I_P$ are sums of the vacuum sector; and transport through both interfaces identifies the defects from $Z(\mathcal N)$ with the defects endable on $B_{\mathcal S}$, including their junction endpoint data. A required part of the problem is to give the coherent categorical version of these endability conditions and prove that it is invariant under the stated equivalence. Determine its intrinsic formulation in monoidal 2-functor language, including which notions of kernel, normality, embedding, dominance and exactness it actually induces. Do not assume the ordinary fusion-category definitions extend unchanged, or assume that a unique maximal anomaly-free full sub-2-category exists.

Seek a description in the finite-group, degree-four cocycle and fusion-category data of the all-boson classification. It must include the finite-group extension benchmark $2\mathrm{Vec}_N\to2\mathrm{Vec}^{p^*\omega}_G\to2\mathrm{Vec}^{\omega}_{G/N}$ and determine the validity and precise hypotheses of the proposed analogous finite-2-group extension, retaining nonsplit Postnikov data. Is the full marked endability/transport invariant complete for the interface equivalence above? If not, exhibit inequivalent finite semisimple marked interfaces with identical proposed invariant and identify the additional junction/coherence datum needed. Classifying gapped phases or abstract fusion 2-categories alone is not this question; neither is a finite enumeration of boundary choices assumed.

As an additional compatibility target, construct the categorical background and relative bulk response data carried by these interfaces and identify their invertible subsector. General SymTFTs can be noninvertible and require categorical state and junction spaces, so scalar local variations, line holonomies and invertible inflow are not asserted to be complete invariants of the full problem. On ordinary backgrounds where the earlier suppliers' hypotheses actually apply, the invertible restriction should reproduce their four-dimensional local BRST class, even-dimensional spin Dirac determinant holonomy, and spin relative-line inflow respectively. Those earlier interfaces neither construct oriented $2+1$-dimensional categorical backgrounds nor prove this extension. No classification, physical realization of an arbitrary abstract diagram, or anomaly-matching theorem is asserted here.

title: Anomaly Matching and Categorical Classification Frontier — Examples

items.title: A mixed-background counterterm shift along RG
items.design_state: B-page worked small-gauge U(1)^3 background counterterm variation on a closed four-torus; verifies equality of the four-dimensional local anomaly classes.
items.statement:
Let $M=T^4$ be a closed flat Euclidean four-torus. Fix three nondynamical $U(1)$ background connections $A_1,A_2,A_3$, each a globally defined real 1-form on the trivial bundle, and allow only gauge transformations $A_i\mapsto A_i+d\lambda_i$ with smooth single-valued periodic real functions $\lambda_i$. Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$, so $[A_i]=$ mass, $[F_i]=$ mass squared, and the functional below is dimensionless. In a declared counterterm scheme, take the allowed local background counterterm

$$
C_k[A_1,A_2,A_3]=\frac{ik}{2\pi}\int_{T^4} A_1\wedge A_2\wedge F_3,
$$

where $F_3=dA_3$ and $k\in\mathbb R$ is a fixed dimensionless coefficient. Suppose an exact background-coupled RG comparison has $W_{\mathrm{UV}}[A_1,A_2,A_3]=W_{\mathrm{IR}}[A_1,A_2,A_3]+C_k[A_1,A_2,A_3]$ on this background domain. Then the two local anomaly representatives differ by

$$
\delta C_k=\frac{ik}{2\pi}\int_{T^4}\bigl(-\lambda_1 F_2\wedge F_3+\lambda_2 F_1\wedge F_3\bigr),\qquad F_i=dA_i,
$$

and therefore define the same local anomaly class modulo the declared counterterms.

items.title: A fixed source breaks the matching symmetry
items.design_state: B-page finite four-dimensional scalar-lattice endpoint with a fixed source; checks explicit breaking and the failure of the theorem hypothesis.
items.statement:
Let $\Lambda_a=(a\mathbb Z/Na\mathbb Z)^4$ be the periodic four-dimensional lattice with $N\geq2$ sites in each direction and spacing $a>0$; each coordinate is taken modulo $Na$. At each site $x$ take a complex scalar $\phi_x$ of mass dimension one. In natural units $c=\hbar=1$, choose a mass $m_0>0$ and a dimensionless coupling $\lambda>0$, and define the finite Euclidean action

$$
S_j[\phi]=a^4\sum_{x\in\Lambda_a}\left(\sum_{\nu=1}^{4}\left|\frac{\phi_{x+a\hat\nu}-\phi_x}{a}\right|^2+m_0^2|\phi_x|^2+\lambda|\phi_x|^4+j(\phi_x+\overline{\phi_x})\right),
$$

where the fixed real source $j\neq0$ has mass dimension three. The finite-dimensional Lebesgue integral converges because the positive quartic term dominates the linear source. The source-free action has a global $U(1)$ transformation $\phi_x\mapsto e^{i\alpha}\phi_x$, but the fixed-source theory does not. Consequently this endpoint fails the exact-symmetry hypothesis of the anomaly-matching theorem; the example asserts no change, absence, or value of an anomaly.
